intro:
A limit asks one question: as $x$ gets close to $a$, what number does $f(x)$ get close to? Here you zoom in on the graph around $x = a$ while a table of values closes in from both sides, and you watch the two one-sided limits arrive.

The gallery holds every way a limit can behave: a hole, a jump, a vertical asymptote, an oscillation that never settles, a point out of place that you can move back, limits at infinity and the squeeze theorem. The continuity checklist ticks as you zoom.
howItWorks:
Each zoom step is ten times closer. The two tracers sit at $x = a - h$ (from the left) and $x = a + h$ (from the right), with $h = 1, 0.1, 0.01, \ldots$; the table adds a row each time, and those rows are exactly where the tracers pass. Every curve, value and table cell comes from the same formula shown under Numbers & setup.

  • Limit from the left $\lim_{x \to a^-} f(x)$: where $f(x)$ heads as $x$ comes up to $a$ from below.
  • Limit from the right $\lim_{x \to a^+} f(x)$: from above.
  • The limit $\lim_{x \to a} f(x)$ exists only when both one-sided limits exist and are equal. It never depends on $f(a)$.
  • Continuous at $a$: $f(a)$ is defined, the limit exists, and they are equal.
